name: HCP Terraform Change Airlock
description:
Governed HCP Terraform run and workspace operations for teams that want AI-assisted infrastructure workflows without silent applies.

WHAT IT DOES: ten focused commands against the real HCP Terraform v2 API: verify the authenticated token, list workspaces, inspect run queues, inspect a run, queue a bounded run, apply/discard/cancel eligible runs, and lock/unlock workspaces.

WHO IT IS FOR: platform, infrastructure, SRE, and engineering teams that want an agent to prepare and operate Terraform changes while preserving a human authorization boundary around every state-changing action.

GOVERNANCE MODEL: every command uses RailCall's vault-only credential path, tight egress to app.terraform.io, preview, and signed receipts. Every mutation is write_requires_approval. Mutations preflight the provider's current state immediately before the write and refuse stale or invalid actions. There are no automatic write retries. A transport failure or ambiguous provider response is reported as UNKNOWN rather than success.

AUTO-APPLY GUARD: HCP Terraform's auto-apply setting applies to API-created runs. To prevent one RailCall approval from silently turning into an unreviewed infrastructure apply, create_run refuses plan_and_apply when workspace auto-apply is enabled. Operators must disable auto-apply or choose a non-applying run mode first.

BOUNDED SURFACE: create_run exposes only plan_and_apply, plan_only, save_plan, and refresh_only. Destroy runs, force-cancel, force-execute, force-unlock, and workspace deletion are intentionally absent from v0.1 because they bypass or weaken normal provider safety paths.

PROVIDER HONESTY: HCP Terraform intentionally returns 404 for both nonexistent and unauthorized resources; the module preserves that ambiguity. Apply/discard/cancel return 'queued_not_completed' after HTTP 202 rather than claiming the action finished. Unlock HTTP 503 is surfaced without auto-retry because HashiCorp documents it as a temporary state-version finalization condition.

commands.title: Verify HCP Terraform connection
commands.description: Resolve the vault token and identify the authenticated HCP Terraform resource without returning the token or account email.

commands.title: List HCP Terraform workspaces
commands.description: List a bounded page of workspaces with lock, auto-apply, execution-mode, Terraform-version, and resource-count context.

commands.title: List HCP Terraform workspace runs
commands.description: Inspect a bounded page of runs, including plan-only runs by default, with status, operation, and currently advertised safe actions.

commands.title: Inspect one HCP Terraform run
commands.description: Read one run and expose provider status, operation, plan/apply references, and the provider's current confirm/discard/cancel capabilities.

commands.title: Queue a governed HCP Terraform run
commands.description: Preflight the workspace, refuse unsafe auto-apply or lock conditions, then queue one non-destroy run using an optional existing configuration version.

commands.title: Apply a confirmed HCP Terraform run
commands.description: Re-read the run, require HCP Terraform to advertise it as confirmable, verify the workspace is unlocked, then queue apply. Returns queued_not_completed after provider HTTP 202.

commands.title: Discard an eligible HCP Terraform run
commands.description: Re-read the run and queue discard only when HCP Terraform currently advertises it as discardable. Returns queued_not_completed after HTTP 202.

commands.title: Cancel an active HCP Terraform run
commands.description: Re-read the run and queue a normal interrupt only when HCP Terraform advertises it as cancelable. Force-cancel is intentionally not exposed.

commands.title: Lock an HCP Terraform workspace
commands.description: Preflight workspace lock state, refuse duplicate locks, then lock with an explicit operator reason.

commands.title: Unlock an HCP Terraform workspace
commands.description: Preflight workspace lock state and request a normal unlock. No force-unlock and no automatic retry on the provider's documented state-finalization 503 condition.
